Cautiously dovish with a stronger risk‑management tilt. The FOMC’s description of moderate growth, strong labor markets, and below‑target inflation aligns with Beige Book signals: districts reported modest overall activity, tight labor markets with wage pressures notably for low-skill and construction roles, solid consumer spending and steady commercial real estate. However, several districts cited slight declines in business activity, mixed-to-softening transportation tied to trade tensions and weaker global demand, constrained home sales with flat new construction, and persistently weak agricultural conditions amid low commodity prices, weather, and trade uncertainty. Lending volumes grew modestly, but layering in SLOOS shows banks tightening standards on C&I and CRE construction/land development with weaker demand—plus some tightening in other consumer credit—which points to more restrictive credit conditions ahead. Together, these reinforce an easing bias and “act as appropriate” guidance: current conditions are mildly positive, but forward risks are tilted to the downside, especially for business investment and trade-exposed sectors.
